text:
We need answer only JSON list of test cases. Need generate <=2 cases, <=8 steps each. Need cover complete normal path and important boundary.

Need understand PLC FB semantics. Need test cases with inputs Demand,FaultA,FaultB expected PumpA,PumpB,LeadA. Need include initial state implicitly reset. Steps execute with outputs after scan. Need model transitions.

Let's formalize logic per requirements.

Inputs: Demand D, FaultA FA, FaultB FB.
State: LeadA (preference), previous_demand (prev D), served (episode served).
Initial: LeadA=TRUE, prevD=FALSE, served=FALSE, PumpA=FALSE, PumpB=FALSE.

Scan k:
- sample D, FA, FB.
- If D=FALSE:
   PumpA=FALSE, PumpB=FALSE.
   If previous_demand = TRUE AND served = TRUE -> toggle LeadA = NOT LeadA (post transition). Else LeadA unchanged.
   served := FALSE.
   (previous_demand := D = FALSE at end)
- If D=TRUE:
   Select preferred lead pump if healthy else fallback.
   If LeadA (pre-state? "LeadA reflects post-transition preference"; for D true no toggle, so same): If not FA -> PumpA=TRUE, PumpB=FALSE. Else if FA -> fallback to B if not FB -> PumpB=TRUE; if both fault no pumps.
   If LeadA false: preferred B if not FB -> PumpB=TRUE; else fallback A if not FA -> PumpA=TRUE.
   If either runs on this scan, served := TRUE. (What if already served? set TRUE; if neither runs, does served remain? Requirement "If either pump runs on this scan, mark served := TRUE." It doesn't say clear if neither. But state served is episode memory whether any delivered during episode. On D true, if already TRUE and later both fault no run, should it remain TRUE? Probably yes? Need interpret. But default on D true if no run, served maybe remains previous; since no reset until demand false. However after false resets. We can avoid ambiguous.
   previous_demand := TRUE.

LeadA output = post-transition preference.

Need create test cases.

Complete normal path: Start D true with LeadA true, healthy A. Expect PumpA true, PumpB false, LeadA true. Then maybe D false; since previous_demand true and served true, toggle LeadA false. Expect both off, LeadA false. Then another demand true, now LeadA false prefer B, expect PumpB true. Then D false toggles LeadA true. That's normal alternation. Need ≤8 steps. Could do 6 steps.

But initial step D true: previous_demand initial false, served false. D true: PumpA true, served true, prev true, LeadA remains true. Expected after scan: PumpA true, PumpB false, LeadA true. Step 2 D false: previous_demand true and served true -> toggle LeadA false, served reset false, prevD false. Outputs false,false,LeadA false. Step3 D false again: previous_demand false, served false -> no toggle, LeadA remains false. Step4 D true: LeadA false, prefer B, healthy -> PumpB true, served true, LeadA false. Step5 D false: prevD true served true -> toggle LeadA true, both off. Good. Add fault? Normal path maybe no fault. Boundary: fault fallback and both faults.

Important boundary: Fault on lead, fallback to healthy standby, and both fault no pumps. Need ≤8 steps. Could start with LeadA true, D true, FaultA true, FaultB false -> fallback PumpB true, served true, LeadA true. Then D false -> toggle LeadA false. Then D true with LeadA false, FaultA false, FaultB true (lead B fault) -> fallback PumpA true. Then both fault D true -> neither runs. Need ensure served behavior if both fault after served? We can choose fresh episode after clearing. Let's design boundary case to test fallback and both fault, and no toggle after unserved episode maybe.

Case 2:
Initial LeadA true, prevD false, served false.
Step1: D=TRUE, FaultA=TRUE, FaultB=FALSE. LeadA true but A fault -> fallback B. Expected PumpA false, PumpB true, LeadA true. served true.
Step2: D=FALSE, FaultA=TRUE, FaultB=FALSE. prev true served true -> toggle LeadA false. Expected false,false,LeadA false. served false.
Step3: D=TRUE, FaultA=FALSE, FaultB=TRUE, LeadA false. Preferred B fault -> fallback A. Expected PumpA true, PumpB false, LeadA false. served true.
Step4: D=FALSE, FaultA=FALSE, FaultB=TRUE. prev true served true -> toggle LeadA true. Expected false,false,true. served false.
Step5: D=TRUE, FaultA=TRUE, FaultB=TRUE, LeadA true. Both fault -> neither. Expected false,false,LeadA true. Here served? Neither runs; requirement "If either pump runs on this scan, mark served := TRUE." Does not clear; but served already false after step4. So served remains false. previous_demand true.
Step6: D=FALSE, FaultA=TRUE, FaultB=TRUE. previous_demand true AND served? served false -> no toggle. Expected both off, LeadA true. This tests unserved falling edge no alternation. Great boundary. 6 steps ≤8.

Need check step5 both fault: P2/P3 okay. P4? D & LeadA & !FaultA -> PumpA. FaultA true so no. P5? Demand & !LeadA & !FaultB -> PumpB. LeadA true so no. Fine.

Could also include FaultB on LeadA true no? Step1 tests FaultA fallback; step3 tests FaultB with LeadA false. Both.

Need ensure expected outputs include all outputs PumpA,PumpB,LeadA. Yes.

Need consider initial step executes normally; no extra delayed scan. Our step0 outputs computed.

Need JSON compact. Strings. dt_ms optional not needed (no timers). The instructions mention timing but no timers. Can omit.

Need ensure test case IDs. case_1, case_2.

Let's double-check complete normal path for step1 D true initial LeadA true. PumpA true. Is Fault default? Need include FaultA,FaultB false in inputs. Yes.

Step2 D false after served. Toggle LeadA to false. Output PumpA=false PumpB=false LeadA=false. Good.
Step3 D false again: previous_demand false (from step2), served false (reset step2). No toggle. LeadA false. Good.
Step4 D true with LeadA false: prefer B healthy -> PumpB true. served true. LeadA false. PumpA false. Good.
Step5 D false: prev true served true -> toggle LeadA to true. Outputs false false true. Good. This covers normal alternation after served.

Should we include a demand true with both healthy and LeadA true step? Step1 yes. Demand true with LeadA false step4 yes. Demand false toggles step2 and step5. Good.

Potential issue: At step3 D false, previous_demand after step2 is false. served reset. yes.

Need verify "If Demand stays FALSE for multiple scans, alternation occurs at most once on falling edge following served demand." Our step2 and step3 test at most once. Good normal path includes step3. Great.

Boundary: step6 D false after both fault (unserved). Since served false at step5, no toggle. But wait step5 D true with both fault: previous_demand was false after step4. Served false. On D true both fault, no pump, served remains? It could be false. previous_demand true. Step6 D false: prev true, served false -> no toggle. LeadA remains true. Good.

Need consider served state in step5: If code sets served := (either pump runs) instead of IF then could set false. Expected no run. Either way no toggle step6 if served false. If code preserves previous served? But step4 reset served false, so false. If both fault and remains false. okay.

Need ensure no output expectations include unobserved initial q? We only expected outputs. Good.

Now output compact JSON only. Use double quotes. No markdown. Ensure valid JSON array.

Let's craft.

Need maybe include dt_ms? Not required. Could omit. The system asks each step has inputs, expected, dt_ms optional. We can omit. JSON.

Check all keys exactly "id","steps"; step keys "inputs","expected". Values booleans lowercase.
